body.statement: Let a finite linear program have a nonempty feasible set and an objective bounded above. Then its Lagrange dual has the same finite value; the primal optimum is attained when its feasible set is compact, and the dual optimum is attained whenever the dual is feasible.

source.locator: Appendix A, finite-dimensional linear-program duality used for sharp bound programs
source.verbatim_statement: If either LP1 or LP2 is feasible and bounded, then so is the other, and opt(LP1) = opt(LP2).

upstream.citation: Luca Trevisan, Stanford CS261 lecture notes, Theorem 6.5 (Strong Duality)

attestation.note: The Russell appendix is the application locator. The supporting theorem text was independently verified in Luca Trevisan, CS261 Lecture 6, publisher-hosted Stanford notes, p. 46 (Theorem 6.5), retrieved 2026-09-14.
